The paper introduces a new strategy for simultaneous acoustic and electromagnetic double-cloaking.
Two operational modes are proposed: blind mode and deaf mode.
Blind mode uses acoustic out-of-shell cloaking (AOSC) and perfect electromagnetic cloaking (EMPC).
Deaf mode uses electromagnetic out-of-shell cloaking (EMOSC) and perfect acoustic cloaking (PAC).
The blind mode arrangement prevents electromagnetic interaction but allows acoustic interaction.
The deaf mode arrangement prevents acoustic interaction but allows electromagnetic interaction.
The dispersive Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method is used for simulations.
For blind mode, AOSC core radius is 0.5 cm, complementary inner radius is 1 cm, complementary outer radius is 1.6 cm, EMPC inner radius is 1.8 cm, and EMPC outer radius is 2 cm.
For deaf mode, EMOSC core radius is 0.5 cm, complementary inner radius is 1 cm, complementary outer radius is 1.6 cm, PAC inner radius is 1.8 cm, and PAC outer radius is 2 cm.
Out-of-shell cloaking allows the object to interact with waves while remaining cloaked.
Perfect cloaking is difficult to achieve in practice.
Cloaking structures require inhomogeneous, anisotropic, and controllable materials.
Metamaterials are often used to achieve the required properties for cloaking.
Transformation theory is used to derive material parameters for cloaking structures.
The method can be generalized to other dual cloaking scenarios.
Multi-cloak invisibility can be used to hide objects from both acoustic and electromagnetic sensors.
The paper references previous work on transformation optics and acoustics.
The approach is demonstrated through simulations of wave scattering patterns.
The blind mode arrangement is shown to preserve the waveform and phase of electromagnetic waves.
The deaf mode arrangement is shown to prevent acoustic waves from penetrating the structure.
The method offers a pathway to multi-physical cloaking beyond just acoustic and electromagnetic waves.
The paper discusses the limitations and challenges of achieving perfect cloaking.
The practical applications include defense, stealth technology, and advanced materials research.
The paper highlights the importance of combining different cloaking methods for multi-physical invisibility.
The results show that the proposed method works for double-cloaking.
